classification.habitat: Subtropical, semi-arid and relatively dry regions
classification.distribution: Drier parts of India, especially Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab and Maharashtra; cultivated in Mandsaur and Neemuch.

identification.description: An erect, branched, tomentose subshrub with ovate leaves, small greenish-yellow flowers and globose red berries enclosed by an enlarged persistent calyx.
identification.whole_plant: Small erect branched shrub or subshrub.
identification.root: The medicinal part is the dried mature root.
identification.leaf: Simple, generally ovate to oblong leaves.
identification.flower: Small greenish-yellow flowers in axillary clusters.
identification.fruit: Globose red berry enclosed by an enlarged persistent calyx.
identification.seed: Numerous, small, reniform, yellowish, enclosed in the orange-red berry.

therapeutics.anupana: Milk or ghee (classically Ashwagandha churna with milk, ghee or lukewarm water).
therapeutics.precautions: Ushna virya; may aggravate Pitta in excess. Use with care alongside sedatives, thyroid hormone, immunosuppressants and antidiabetic drugs. Rare liver injury has been reported with concentrated extracts.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, in hyperthyroidism, and in states of high Ama or severe Pitta aggravation.

shlokas:
गन्धान्ता वाजिनामादिरश्वगन्धा हयाह्वया ।
वराहकर्णी वरदा बलदा कुष्ठगन्धिनी ॥
अश्वगन्धाऽनिलश्लेष्मश्वित्रशोथक्षयापहा ।
बल्या रसायनी तिक्ता कषायोष्णाऽतिशुक्रला ॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Guduchyadi Varga, verses 161–162 in the searchable recension; edition numbering may vary.
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The root contains steroidal lactones (withanolides) and several alkaloids, which are regarded as its main active groups.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is a powerful adaptogen. It reduces stress, increases strength, and supports reproductive and nervous systems.
recognized_uses: Anidra and stress-related complaints (rasayana, medhya use)
modern_information.safety_notes: Usually well tolerated; drowsiness and gastric upset can occur. Avoid in pregnancy and hyperthyroidism, and stop if signs of liver injury appear.

Formulations: Ashwagandharishta, Ashwagandhadi Lehya, Balashwagandhalakshadi Taila
Dose: churna 3–6 g, with milk or ghee
